races.name: Ray And Eileen Mclean Memorial EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Jw 4x4 Northallerton Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Heineken 0% Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hover On The Wind
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with two recent course-and-distance wins (form 117), going is fine, but Paul Midgley fields three horses here and this one's natural hold-up style means it will likely find itself further back than those back-to-back wins suggest — the race shape puts it out of its comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Managing Director
runners_data.note: Strong-travelling front-runner for Geoff Oldroyd with a win at 5f on good and a clear record of racing from the front; likely to press Equity Law hard throughout, but a single runner for trainer in 14 days (0/1) and a tendency to fade when headed late is the risk.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent type who scored last time at 5f on good, and Shane Gray keeps it simple from a handy position; trainer Tristan Davidson's 0/6 in 14 days tempers enthusiasm, and the age means peak form windows matter — in-form but vulnerable if the pace is genuinely fierce.

runners_data.name: Winchurch
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's four-year-old has won twice at 5f and holds hold-up/rear-running tendencies, yet his sim-going record is modest (5/15); Tom Eaves gets the ride for a trainer with one 14-day winner from 22 and the 15th-place run at 6f on good last time is easy to dismiss — 5f on good is the right conditions.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's second string has an outstanding 5f good-ground profile (sim-going 11/15, 3 wins) and is the classiest of the hold-up trio; genuinely races from behind and will be further back than ideal, but Luke Morris has the experience to time a run — form figures 131214 confirm consistency.

runners_data.name: Equity Law
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Tim Easterby, who is in red-hot 14-day form (5/69), wearing headgear and returning after 54 days off with a recent 5f win on good ground; if she can shrug off Managing Director's challenge in the opening exchanges, she has every chance of lasting to the line.

runners_data.name: Moulin Booj
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 81, Daniel Tudhope booked, and a record of 1-2-5-2-3 across 5f on good — outstanding profile for this shape; the three-day turnaround is the only flag, though George Scott has 2/12 in 14 days and the horse's recent winning form suggests it is in excellent nick.

runners_data.name: Accrual
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's five-year-old has a single sim-going qualified run (1/15, one win) which is a stark flag on this surface and going combination despite a recent third; William Pyle takes the ride and the inconsistent form string (U53051) with a U last time out makes this a speculative runner at best.

runners_data.name: Emerald Harmony
runners_data.note: Midgley's third runner in this race, a five-year-old with decent recent form (031236) and a good sim-going record (11/15); David Nolan rides and the horse has a 5f good-ground win to its name, but — like the stable's other two runners — its natural instinct to race from the rear is likely to be frustrated by the weight of hold-up types in this field, reducing its chance below its bare form.

races.paceDynamic: Equity Law and Managing Director are the two confirmed front-runners and will clash for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested early gallop over Thirsk's straight five furlongs on good ground. Equity Law, who carries headgear and has Tim Easterby's strong recent form behind her, is likely to edge ahead, but Managing Director will press throughout, ensuring the pace is honest rather than suicidal — this is not a race where either will back off. That contested lead on a flat, fair track typically sets it up for horses who can travel prominently and pick up, rather than those having to make up large amounts of ground from deep. This race shape favours hold-up horses who can secure a prominent pitch, but the field contains more true hold-up types than the race can accommodate — Emerald Harmony, Rock Of England, and Hover On The Wind are genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map and are unlikely to get their natural position; of those three, Rock Of England's superior sim-going record and class gives it the best chance of threading through late, with Moulin Booj — arriving on a short turnaround but carrying the highest OR and boasting the strongest recent record on good ground — the most likely beneficiary of a race run to suit prominent-to-mid types.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Equity Law and Managing Director fight for the lead and set a genuine pace that softens the front two, allowing a prominent or mid-division horse to surge through
scenarios.body: Equity Law and Managing Director burn each other up across the first two furlongs, leaving the race open to horses who travel in the first half of the field without over-committing; Moulin Booj, with the highest OR and a proven good-ground record over 5f, and Rock Of England, the classiest of the closers, are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Equity Law escapes the duel early and establishes a comfortable lead, controlling tempo and quickening away
scenarios.body: Equity Law has recent winning form at 5f on good, carries headgear, and Easterby's 5/69 14-day strike rate signals the stable is firing; if she gets first run and dictates, her rivals may simply not have the room to reel her in on this flat track

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is high enough and the field fans wide late, allowing a genuine closer to find daylight and pick up strongly
scenarios.body: Moulin Booj or Winchurch, who both have strong good-ground 5f profiles, could pounce if the front-runners tie each other up completely; however, Emerald Harmony and Hover On The Wind, though redistributed back into midfield, face the real risk of being further back than ideal and needing everything to go perfectly

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel collapses unusually fast and an unexpected finisher catches the field flat-footed in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Our Absent Friends, who has a recent course win at 5f on good and is a straightforward prominent type, or Accrual, back on a fast surface after mixed going, could emerge if the market leaders underperform; this is the least likely shape given the honest, structured pace and the quality of horses higher in the market

watchPoints.text: Equity Law and Managing Director — watch whether either horse blinks in the first furlong; if Managing Director presses hard from stall to two furlongs, both may be compromised and the race opens dramatically for Moulin Booj.

Rock Of England, Hover On The Wind, and Emerald Harmony — all three Paul Midgley runners are natural closers competing for the same late ground; congestion in the final furlong is a real risk and backers of any of the three should note they may hamper each other.

Moulin Booj — three days since last run is the single concern for the highest-rated horse in the field; watch the market move and pre-race demeanour, as Tudhope booking for an in-form George Scott runner on a tight turnaround usually signals confidence rather than doubt.
Accrual — only one qualifying run on today's going out of fifteen career starts on similar ground is a significant data point; if the market drifts, take the hint.

Our Absent Friends — the eight-year-old's course-and-distance win last time is eye-catching, but trainer Tristan Davidson's 0/6 in 14 days means the stable is not in a purple patch; watch if Shane Gray rides with urgency early or settles, which will signal whether the team expects a big run.

races.name: Andrew Seaton Celebration Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Enchant
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for K.R. Burke with James Doyle in the saddle — the 1W1P record in similar going is encouraging but only two runs on that surface makes projection difficult; 61 days off means fitness is the key question, but Burke's 6/37 T14 strike rate suggests the stable is in fair form.

runners_data.name: Return Of The Gods
runners_data.note: Clear front-runner whose ability to dictate on good ground is the defining tactical factor in this race; Tudhope is a shrewd handler of pace horses, though the [STYLE_FIT] tag signals that any scenario forcing it off the front would materially reduce its chance — it must get to the lead cleanly.

runners_data.name: Zarvali
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's hold-up performer arrives on a seven-day turnaround in decent form after a win over this course and distance on good ground; nine runs on similar ground producing one win and three places suggests consistency, though the true rear-of-field position may be further back than the pace map reflects.

runners_data.name: Substance
runners_data.note: Wears headgear and races from hold-up, returning after 70 days off for Mark Walford; the 1W2P record on similar going is positive and the win over 8f suggests stamina won't be an issue stepping back to 7f, though the layoff and Jack Garritty claiming could be a limiting factor.

runners_data.name: Raging Raj
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves rides this prominent racer who won over 7f on good ground and has placed at 8f — the stamina base is solid and the forward position in a genuine pace scenario suits; Michael Herrington's 3/9 T14 strike rate is fair, and a repeat of the run that produced a win over this trip is entirely possible.

runners_data.name: Shadow Run
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by profile whose true running style is further back than the midfield position shown — placed into midfield on the map because the field is stacked with hold-up types, but Luke Morris should be aware the horse may find itself further rear than ideal; the [STYLE_FIT] note tempers confidence, and stepping up from 5f to 7f is a significant jump in trip.

runners_data.name: Derrygarran Lad
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's three-run maiden who has placed all three times without winning — all runs have come on good or standard going, and the trip and conditions are within the comfort zone; wears headgear and is ridden by Ryan Sexton, with consistency the calling card but a first win still to materialise.

runners_data.name: Indefensible
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears' prominent racer with a solid form string including a win over this course and distance — six runs on similar ground with 1W4P shows reliability, and Harry Russell's low-key booking doesn't diminish what is arguably one of the most course-and-distance consistent profiles in the field; should sit close to the pace throughout.

races.paceDynamic: Return Of The Gods is the one confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with Raging Raj and Indefensible likely to press forward from a prominent position, the pace should be genuine and consistent throughout the seven furlongs on good ground at Thirsk. Return Of The Gods has the racing style to dictate from the front, but with Raging Raj and Indefensible tracking closely, they will collectively set an honest gallop rather than an uncontested dawdle, meaning the pace is unlikely to be either too slow or truly brutal. Shadow Run is a genuine hold-up type who has been mapped to midfield because the field contains more horses wanting to race at the rear than the pace map can accommodate at that position, meaning its true stalking position may be further back than shown. This race shape — a genuinely run 7f on good turf with a clear pace hierarchy — favours horses who can travel prominently or make a sustained mid-race move, giving the edge to prominent racers who can handle a true pace without being consumed by it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Return Of The Gods and Raging Raj set a genuine but controlled gallop and the field strings out naturally, allowing the pace-setters and prominent racers to control the race from start to finish.
scenarios.body: Return Of The Gods leads at a sustainable clip with Raging Raj and Indefensible sitting close, and the race becomes a test of stamina and class as they kick on from two furlongs out; prominent horses who handle a true pace without fading are at a clear advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Quicken Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to string out the field and the front-runners sustain their effort into the final two furlongs, denying closers any momentum.
scenarios.body: Raging Raj and Indefensible use their prominent positions to kick on decisively when Return Of The Gods begins to tire, with the race settled before any hold-up horse can land a blow; this shape rewards horses who combine tactical speed with genuine 7f stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions are genuinely hot and the prominent racers burn each other out, leaving the hold-up horses with a wall of tired rivals to pass in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Zarvali or Substance, carrying hold-up profiles, are the most likely beneficiaries if the pace collapses in the final furlong; however, both Shadow Run's redistribution and the genuinely modest nature of the pace make this a less probable shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Horse Improves
scenarios.trigger: If Enchant or Derrygarran Lad, both with limited form lines, produce career-best efforts as unexposed three-year-olds on a straightforward gallop.
scenarios.body: Enchant has shown ability on good ground over this course and distance combination and could improve sharply from a lightly raced profile; Derrygarran Lad has placed consistently but lacks a win and would need the pace to set up perfectly from mid-to-rear.

watchPoints.text: Return Of The Gods must break cleanly and establish the lead immediately — if Raging Raj or Indefensible jump faster and take the rail, the entire race dynamic changes and Return Of The Gods is racing out of role.

Shadow Run's true running position may be significantly further back than the race map indicates — watch where Luke Morris settles it in the early stages, as an overly wide or deep position on a straight seven could cost it any realistic winning chance.

Enchant's 61-day absence for K.R. Burke is the critical unknown — if the stable has prepared it well the form lines are very solid, but a ring-rusty effort would not be a surprise given the limited runs on its card.

Zarvali arrives on a seven-day turnaround after finishing tenth at Newmarket — Roger Fell regularly runs horses back quickly, but the form behind that effort and the step back in class here means it merits watching for early signs of whether it travels freely or labours.

The Thirsk 7f going report confirms Good all day — no bias concern, but the flat, straight track will ensure the honest pace from Return Of The Gods and Raging Raj is felt throughout the field, particularly by any horse that travels prominently but lacks the stamina to see out the trip.

races.name: Malton Marquees Racing Through The Summer Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Roaring Ralph
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two wins and three places from five runs on similar Good turf, proven at 8f, fitter for a recent run 21 days ago and wears a bridle — needs to win the scrum for position early.

runners_data.name: Style Of Life
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; returns from 91 days off which is the key query, but Bethell's small yard has a 1/8 recent record and she has gone 2W 4P from seven attempts on similar ground — everything depends on her fitness holding.

runners_data.name: Bloodsweatandtyres
runners_data.note: Prominent type with just one similar-going run (5th of 5) to reference at 8f, her recent form is a run of five and ten on Tapeta; fitness is fine at 18 days but the move to Good turf from all-weather surfaces is a significant query.

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.note: Highly consistent place-getter — 1W 3P from five runs at 8f on Good, including three seconds in a row and a third; Mulrennan is a positive booking, the bridle headgear helps, and a 6-day turnaround for Makin (1/12) suggests he is ready to go.

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type who has placed twice in three Good-ground mile runs this term; Declan Carroll's yard is 0/8 in 14 days so trainer angle is cold, but Zak Wheatley keeps costs low and the mare's 2nd last time out at the trip is live form.

runners_data.name: Harswell Ruby
runners_data.note: Prominent filly with a tidy record of 1W 2P from ten similar-going runs, placed twice at 8f on Good recently; Joanna Mason is a booking that matters on northern tracks and the horse is fresh enough after 16 days.

runners_data.name: Donna Nook
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won at 8f on Good and has placed in 2/3 subsequent tries at the trip; Tudhope is a major booking upgrade for O'Meara (9/53 in 14 days), and she wears a tongue-tie and visor combination that has been on for the better runs.

runners_data.name: Green Pursuit
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping up from 7f to 8f, all of whose recent form has been on Soft or Good-to-Soft; Good ground on turf is a genuine step into the unknown for this gelding, and 61 days off adds further caution.

runners_data.name: Jesmond Dawn
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who is 1W 3P from five runs on similar Good ground at the trip — excellent going record; Oliver Stammers is a 5lb claimer but the form is solid and 27 days since a fifth is a normal freshener.

runners_data.name: Up The Jazz
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type — 1W 5P from ten Good-ground runs at the mile — who has won at this exact course and distance; Fahey yard is active (4/28 T14), and Ethan Tindall (5lb claim) offsets a favourable weight, making this a runner with real tactical credentials even mapped into midfield.

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with 1W 5P from fourteen runs on Good going at 8f — he runs here almost every week; form figures of 0-5-0-8-5-3 are functional rather than exciting, but Oisin Orr is an excellent booking for a horse with known late tendencies on this track.

runners_data.name: Mount King
runners_data.note: In-form at home — 2W 4P from ten Good-ground runs and a winner last time out — but is a genuine hold-up type by nature whose closing run will be compromised if he is squeezed into midfield by the prominent traffic; Easterby's yard is firing (5/69 T14) and the bridle headgear is familiar.

runners_data.name: Travis
runners_data.note: A confirmed closer whose best form shows 1W 4P from nine Good-ground starts with a pattern of finishing 3rd-3rd-3rd recently; Geoffrey Harker's yard is quiet (0/3 T14) and the horse's natural rearward style will be difficult to execute from a midfield slot in this congested field.

runners_data.name: Palmarian
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's hold-up mare carries headgear (hood) and has a win and a second from eight Good-ground outings; she won at 8f on Good last time and has natural finishing pace, but her true closer profile is undermined by being pushed into a midfield starting point in this traffic-heavy field.

runners_data.name: Miss Willows
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old hold-up mare returning after 59 days off for a quiet yard (0/6 T14); her best form is on softer or sounder tracks and she has two wins and two places from ten Good-ground starts, but the layoff, modest trainer stats and compromised running position all work against her.

races.paceDynamic: Style Of Life is the lone confirmed front-runner and, coming off a 91-day break, will be allowed to dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over this flat Thirsk mile — no genuine rival is likely to pressure her early enough to force a true test of stamina. Behind her, Roaring Ralph, Bloodsweatandtyres, Military Leader, Harswell Ruby, Donna Nook and Jesmond Dawn all want prominent positions, creating a wall of pace hunters that will jostle for the first three furlongs and generate traffic compression from the 3f pole home. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can naturally accommodate at the rear — Mount King, Travis, Palmarian and Miss Willows are genuine closers by nature but will be shuffled into a midfield no-man's-land where their finishing kicks may be partially negated. With a single front-runner setting a measured, unhurried tempo and a cluttered prominent group unable to fully stretch the pace, this race shape strongly favours hold-up runners who can find a clear route from 2f out and prominent racers with proven tactical speed on Good turf — patient, well-positioned midfield types with a sharp turn of foot stand to benefit most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Style Of Life bowls along at a comfortable solo gallop and the prominent pack fails to apply any sustained pressure before the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Style Of Life sets her own fractions unchallenged, and horses who stalked close without burning energy in the scrum — particularly Military Leader and Jesmond Dawn — are best placed to pounce as she ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramblers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the six-strong prominent group sorts itself out quickly and produces a competitive but not ruinous pace that rewards those who secured a handy berth from wide draws.
scenarios.body: Roaring Ralph and Donna Nook, both proven in similar conditions and OR brackets, slot in behind the leader and benefit from the pace being genuine enough to stop any lone front-runner kicking clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Clears Late, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent bunch causes sustained interference and ties itself in knots from 3f out, gifting a clean late run to the genuine hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Up The Jazz and Alessia Fernanda, both natural closers with Good-ground form at the trip, would be the primary beneficiaries if gaps appear late on a flat track that favours sustained galloping runs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scenario, Big Field Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion sparks crowding and interference, several fancied runners miss their chance and a lightly-weighted outsider sneaks through.
scenarios.body: With 15 runners and six prominent types all seeking the same strip of ground, a clean-run hold-up runner at a long price — such as Travis or Palmarian — could benefit from the carnage, though both are racing out of their ideal rail-hugging role.

watchPoints.text: Style Of Life's 91-day layoff is the race's pivotal variable — if she ties up in the final furlong, the six prominent horses directly behind her will collide in a wall of interference at a critical moment.

Roaring Ralph, Bloodsweatandtyres, Military Leader, Harswell Ruby, Donna Nook and Jesmond Dawn all want the same prominent strip of ground — watch for bumping and crowding in the first two furlongs as six horses cannot all sit second.
Mount King and Palmarian are genuine closers by ability but will likely be trapped in mid-division traffic from 3f out — any horse drawn near them faces being pocketed at the most critical stage.

Daniel Tudhope's booking for Donna Nook (O'Meara 9/53 in 14 days) stands out as the most significant jockey upgrade in the race — watch her position from the break as Tudhope will move to a handy spot quickly.

Up The Jazz ran 1st, 2nd and 3rd across the last three course starts at Thirsk over the mile — course-specific form at this exact track is a concrete edge worth tracking as the field rounds the final bend.

races.name: Birra Moretti Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Prince Achille
runners_data.note: Off the track 148 days — the extended absence is the primary concern for a seven-year-old with a modest recent form string of 4578, and his best similar-going return shows just one place from six runs over comparable trips; a true hold-up horse who will need the race to fall apart late to get involved.

runners_data.name: Halimede
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott has placed this three-year-old with precision, winning back-to-back over 12f-13f on standard and good ground, and the step up to 1m4f at Thirsk looks a logical progression; she is a genuine hold-up type by inclination but will be drawn to the front by default here — her fade-in-finish flag means the final two furlongs will define her chance.

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: Has won twice at 10f on good and soft ground and placed at 12f, showing solid staying credentials at OR 56; a genuine deep hold-up type who is likely to push forward into midfield here simply because the race shape provides no natural cover — trainer Philip Kirby is 0/16 in the last 14 days, adding a minor negative yard angle, and the style-fit discount (0.91) reflects the positional compromise.

races.paceDynamic: Halimede is the only genuine pace-setter in this three-runner field, and despite being a natural hold-up horse by style, will be redistributed to the front given the complete absence of any other confirmed leader — she is effectively gifted an uncontested, pressure-free lead over 1m4f on good ground at Thirsk. With Recobella and Prince Achille both hold-up types by inclination, Halimede can control every fraction from flag to finish, setting a tempo entirely of her own choosing before her known tendency to fade late becomes the critical question. The field holds more true hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, meaning Recobella is most likely to push forward into a midfield berth rather than her natural deeper position. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner or prominent racer who can dictate a sustainable gallop — Halimede's recent back-to-back wins over 12f-13f on good-to-standard ground and her trainer Sir Mark Prescott's renowned ability to place horses with surgical precision make the controlled-lead profile the dominant shape to assess against.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Halimede Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Halimede bowls along at a measured pace and neither rival has the tactical speed to challenge her lead.
scenarios.body: Halimede sets a sustainable tempo over the 1m4f trip, her two recent wins at 12f-13f on similar ground providing strong evidence she stays well when allowed to race on her own terms; the hold-up pair behind face the task of pegging back a horse that has already dictated the race and can time her own finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Halimede's known tendency to fade in the final furlong catches up with her after a solo lead and the hold-up pair arrive with a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: Prince Achille or Recobella, tracking at a respectful distance, may pick up the pieces if Halimede ties up in the closing stages; Recobella's two wins at 10f-12f on good and soft ground suggest she has the stamina and change of gear to capitalise if the leader weakens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Rear Pair Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Halimede fades severely and both hold-up rivals produce strong finishes simultaneously, creating a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: Prince Achille, dropping back to a trip he has run respectably over, and Recobella both arriving late could produce an open battle for the spoils; however, Prince Achille's 148-day absence and modest recent form (4578) make this scenario reliant on significant improvement.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Field Strings Out
scenarios.trigger: If Halimede is hustled along faster than intended, perhaps through Recobella pushing forward early, turning it into a war of attrition.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected gallop would stretch the field and favour whichever horse handles the pace best over the distance; Recobella's genuine stamina profile at 10f-12f gives her a marginal edge in this scenario, though her redistribution out of true hold-up role means this shape remains unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Watch Halimede in the final two furlongs — her "fades in finish" tag is the single biggest risk in this race and will determine whether the hold-up pair can reel her in.
Watch whether Recobella pushes forward early from her natural hold-up position; if she contests the lead it could inject unwanted pace and compromise Halimede's controlled tempo.

Prince Achille returns from 148 days off — watch for signs of ring-rustiness in the early stages, as a hold-up horse needing a true run of pace to arrive late will be badly placed if the race is falsely run.

Watch Halimede's sectionals through the middle portion of the race — if Sir Mark Prescott has drilled her to conserve energy over the trip, a strong penultimate furlong would signal she has the race won before the final bend.

races.review_reason: style/note conflict — check before trusting notes
